categories.main_business_segments: OHSHO FOOD SERVICE CORP. operates primarily in the Chinese cuisine restaurant business, focusing on both directly managed restaurant chains and the sale of Chinese food ingredients to franchise (FC) stores. The company also includes subsidiaries for overseas restaurant operations (Taiwan) and food processing/cleaning services (Japan).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company emphasizes high-quality, fresh ingredients, with a focus on handmade cooking at each restaurant. Production is supported by company-owned factories that manufacture key items such as gyoza (dumplings), noodles, and other food products, using modernized production lines and strict quality control systems, including ISO9001 and FSSC22000 certifications.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The main customers are general consumers seeking affordable and tasty Chinese cuisine, with a broad demographic appeal including families, students, and office workers. The company also serves franchisees as customers for food ingredients and support services, and has a growing presence in the takeout and delivery market.
categories.geographic_coverage: OHSHO operates 728 stores (as of March 2025), with a strong presence throughout Japan, especially in the Kansai, Kanto, and Chubu regions. The company also has two directly managed stores in Taiwan and is exploring further overseas expansion.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company is positioned downstream in the supply chain as a restaurant operator, but also has midstream activities through its food manufacturing plants supplying both its own stores and franchisees. It controls much of its supply chain from ingredient procurement to final food service.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include continuous improvement of product quality (notably gyoza and noodles), digital transformation (DX) for operational efficiency and customer convenience, aggressive store investment (including direct management of former FC stores), and sustainability initiatives such as CO2 reduction and food recycling. The company invests heavily in human capital and brand enhancement, but does not have a formal R&D division.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through direct sales of food and beverages at company-operated restaurants, with additional income from the sale of food ingredients and materials to franchisees. Other revenue streams include franchise fees, takeout/delivery services, and limited overseas operations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other major Japanese restaurant chains specializing in Chinese cuisine and casual dining, such as Bamiyan (Skylark Group) and Hidakaya. OHSHO is a market leader in the gyoza restaurant segment, known for its scale, brand recognition, and high profitability.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated sales reached 111.0 billion yen, with operating profit of 10.9 billion yen and net profit of 8.1 billion yen. The company has demonstrated steady growth, achieving record-high sales and profits for four consecutive years, and maintains a strong financial position with a high equity ratio (76.8%).
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: OHSHO differentiates itself through its commitment to 'delicious, fast, and affordable' handmade Chinese cuisine, high ingredient quality (notably domestic sourcing), and a unique customer experience combining comfortable dining spaces and warm service. The company also emphasizes operational excellence, digital convenience, and a strong, trusted brand built over more than 50 years.
